classification.difficultyReason: The hardest configuration requires introducing auxiliary parallel lines at successive bends, transferring angles and deciding which angles to subtract to obtain the final angle.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Triangle SLM between two oblique parallel lines; all seven printed point labels and both parallel marks retained. Ordinary source blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: K,L,M,N are collinear; R,S,T are collinear; LN is parallel to RT. Angle LSM is 36 degrees, MST is 32 degrees, LMS is alpha and KLS is beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknowns remain symbolic; no answers appear.

spec.description: Broken line A–B–O–G–F. Preserve the original absence of parallel-arrow marks; the authorised parallel given appears in editable prompt text.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABO is 38 degrees, OGF is 70 degrees and BOG is alpha; the editorial clarification states BA parallel GF.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and alpha are drawn.

answer.short:
$\alpha=108^\circ$.

Draw a line through $O$ parallel to $BA$ and $GF$.
answer.worked:
Draw a line through $O$ parallel to $BA$ and $GF$. The leftward ray splits $\alpha$ into angles of $38^\circ$ and $70^\circ$ by alternate angles.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=38^\circ+70^\circ\\\alpha&=108^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Stepped connector between two horizontal parallel lines. Horizontal lines have double arrows; descending segments have single arrows. Junctions on horizontal lines remain unnamed.
spec.mathematics: Both pairs of marked lines are parallel; 86 degrees is below the upper line to the left of its descending segment, and alpha is above the lower line to the left of its ascending ray.

answer.worked:
Extend the sloping segment through $O$ below $LM$. Using both pairs of parallel lines, the angle below $LM$ and to the left of this extension is $86^\circ$ (corresponding angles). It is adjacent to $\alpha$ on a straight line.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-86^\circ\\\alpha&=94^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Alternating zigzag D–E–N–T–A–L with the two outer segments parallel and matching arrow marks.
spec.mathematics: DEN is 70 degrees, ENT is 120 degrees, NTA is 140 degrees and TAL is alpha; DE parallel AL.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three given angles and alpha are visible.

answer.short:
$\alpha=90^\circ$.

Use auxiliary lines parallel to $DE$ and $AL$.
answer.worked:
Through $N$ and $T$, draw lines parallel to $DE$. At $N$, the angle between $NE$ and the downward parallel ray is $70^\circ$ (alternate angles), leaving $120^\circ-70^\circ=50^\circ$ between that ray and $NT$. At $T$, the angle between $TN$ and the upward parallel ray is $50^\circ$ (alternate angles). Hence the angle between that upward ray and $TA$ is $140^\circ-50^\circ=90^\circ$. By alternate angles with $AL$,
$$\alpha=90^\circ.$$

spec.description: Two sloping rays meet at Y below two parallel horizontal lines, with all seven source point names and parallel marks.
spec.mathematics: Upper-left angle at N is 70 degrees; upper-right angle at O is 65 degrees; gamma is upper-right at C, beta lower-left at E and alpha at Y.

answer.worked:
The upper-right angle at $E$ is $65^\circ$ (corresponding angles), so $\beta=65^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles). The upper-left angle at $C$ is $70^\circ$ (corresponding angles).
$$\begin{align*}\gamma&=180^\circ-70^\circ\\\gamma&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angle at $N$ in $\triangle NYE$ is $70^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-70^\circ-65^\circ\\\alpha&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle GFH between horizontal parallel lines. GF extends to J; FH extends to I and below H. All source labels and single parallel arrows retained.
spec.mathematics: JFB is 45 degrees, CHG is 34 degrees and FGH is alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: Only givens and alpha are visible.

answer.worked:
Through $G$, draw a line parallel to $AB$ and $CD$. Its rightward ray splits $\alpha$ into $45^\circ$ (corresponding angles) and $34^\circ$ (alternate angles).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=45^\circ+34^\circ\\\alpha&=79^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral ETIK, with a right-angle square at K and the three printed angle labels.
spec.mathematics: E is 60 degrees, K is 90 degrees, I is 120 degrees and T is alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: Alpha is not evaluated in the question.

answer.worked:
The interior angles of quadrilateral $ETIK$ sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=360^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ-120^\circ\\\alpha&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Quadrilateral QUAD with each indicated side extension, eight point labels and four exterior-angle labels.
spec.mathematics: W,Q,U are collinear; A,U,X are collinear; Q,D,Z are collinear; D,A,Y are collinear. WQD is 86 degrees, QUX is 110 degrees, ZDA is 100 degrees and UAY is alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three given exterior angles and alpha are shown.

answer.short:
$\alpha=64^\circ$.

Find the adjacent interior angles, then use the quadrilateral angle sum.
answer.worked:
Adjacent angles on each straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle DQU&=180^\circ-86^\circ=94^\circ\\\angle QUA&=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ\\\angle QDA&=180^\circ-100^\circ=80^\circ\end{align*}$$
Using the angle sum of quadrilateral $QUAD$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle UAD&=360^\circ-94^\circ-70^\circ-80^\circ\\\angle UAD&=116^\circ\\\alpha&=180^\circ-116^\circ\\\alpha&=64^\circ\end{align*}$$
